title: The over-refusal link: do safety steering vectors catastrophically block dual-use medical/security questions?

original_idea.body: Curate ~80 dual-use prompts plus clearly-harmful/benign controls; apply a safety steering vector and measure over-refusal on the ambiguous middle; forward passes.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Over-refusal of dual-use knowledge is real but more usability harm; indirect catastrophic-risk link (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Curated prompts + fixed-strength steering + refusal scoring; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear success criterion (dual-use over-refusal rate) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Diffuse over-refusal eval, lab-underweighted, externally doable (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Curated prompts + forward passes, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Over-refusal studied; steering dual-use-middle slice partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Dual-use-middle steering slice may be partly open.
